title: Example: Inserting Duplicate Values to id Column

blocks.content: Example: Inserting Duplicate Values to id Column
Suppose you try to insert two books, "The Great Gatsby" and "Harry Potter", into the Books table with the same id value of 1.

1CREATE TABLE Books (
2    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
3    title VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
4    book_code VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE,
5    publisher VARCHAR(100)
6);
7
8INSERT INTO Books (id, title, book_code, publisher)
9VALUES (1, 'The Great Gatsby', 'BC123', 'ABC Publishing');
10
11INSERT INTO Books (id, title, book_code, publisher)
12VALUES (1, 'Harry Potter', 'BC456', 'XYZ Publishing');
Here, the code returns a unique constraint error, confirming that the primary key must be unique.
Similarly, you cannot insert a NULL value in the primary key, i.e., the id column.

-- This statement will produce an error 
--  because primary key columns cannot have NULL values.
INSERT INTO Books (id, title, book_code, publisher)
VALUES (NULL, 'To Kill a Mockingbird', 'BC789', 'Penguin Books');
